scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): a two-view response that measures a society by the welfare of all while granting that collective strength matters; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Every society must decide whether to value its overall power or the well-being of each citizen.
Some believe a society must put its overall success before the well-being of individuals, while others believe its health can only be measured by the welfare of all its people.
I lean toward the second view, but I accept that a society's collective strength also matters for its people.
First, the well-being of ordinary people is the truest measure of a society's success.
A nation that grows rich or powerful while its people suffer has not truly succeeded.
For example, a country with a strong army but hungry citizens has failed at its most basic task.
This shows that overall success means little if it does not reach the people themselves.
A society exists, after all, to serve the lives of the individuals who make it up.
When every citizen can live decently, the society as a whole is genuinely strong.
For these reasons, I believe the welfare of all is the better measure of success.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why collective strength matters too

sentences.text: Second, however, the opposing view rightly notes that a society's overall success also matters.
At times a nation must act for the common good, even at a cost to particular individuals.
Consider a country that raises taxes or asks for sacrifice in wartime to protect everyone's future.
Such efforts show that the strength of the whole can be needed to protect each person within it.
When a society is too weak to defend or support itself, it cannot protect the welfare of anyone.
Collective success and individual welfare, in truth, depend on each other.
Both views, then, capture something a wise society must keep in balance.
In conclusion, I believe a society is best measured by the welfare of all its people.
But its overall strength matters too, since a weak society cannot protect anyone.
The wisest society pursues its collective success precisely in order to serve the lives of its citizens.
